name.description: The name of the logging sink. Must be unique within the billing account.
name.rationale: Sink names should clearly indicate purpose and destination to ensure proper management and auditability of log export configurations.
name.compliant: Descriptive names following organizational naming conventions (e.g., security-logs-to-bq, audit-logs-to-cs)
name.non-compliant: Generic or unclear names that don't indicate sink purpose or destination

billing_account.description: The billing account to which the logging sink applies.
billing_account.rationale: Billing account selection ensures the sink is applied to the correct organizational scope and impacts cost management and access controls.
billing_account.compliant: Proper billing account ID with appropriate access controls

destination.description: Cloud Storage bucket, a PubSub topic, a BigQuery dataset or a Cloud Logging bucket. Examples: - `storage.googleapis.com/[GCS_BUCKET]` - `bigquery.googleapis.com/projects/[PROJECT_ID]/datasets/[DATASET]` - `pubsub.googleapis.com/projects/[PROJECT_ID]/topics/[TOPIC_ID]` - `logging.googleapis.com/projects/[PROJECT_ID]]/locations/global/buckets/[BUCKET_ID]` The writer associated with the sink must have access to write to the above resource.
destination.rationale: Destination selection impacts data security, access controls, and compliance with data residency requirements. Must be properly secured destinations.
destination.compliant: Properly secured destinations with appropriate access controls and encryption
destination.non-compliant: Unsecured or unauthorized destinations, public buckets, or improperly configured endpoints

filter.description: The filter that determines which log entries to include in the sink. See [Advanced Log Filters](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/view/advanced_filters) for information on how to write a filter.
filter.rationale: Filter criteria must ensure all required security and compliance logs are captured while avoiding unnecessary data export that could increase risk.
filter.compliant: Comprehensive filters that capture all required security and compliance logs
filter.non-compliant: Overly restrictive filters that miss critical security logs or overly broad filters that export unnecessary data

description.description: A description of the sink's purpose, what log data it exports, and where it sends the data.
description.rationale: Clear descriptions help ensure proper understanding of log data flows, destinations, and purposes for security monitoring and compliance.
description.compliant: Detailed description of sink purpose, data content, and destination
description.non-compliant: Missing or vague descriptions that obscure sink purposes and data flows

disabled.description: Whether the sink is disabled. If true, the sink does not export any log entries.
disabled.rationale: Sink status should be carefully managed to ensure critical log exports remain active for security monitoring and compliance requirements.
disabled.compliant: false (for required security and compliance log exports)
disabled.non-compliant: true (for sinks that should be active per security policy)

bigquery_options.description: Options that affect sinks exporting data to BigQuery.
bigquery_options.rationale: BigQuery options impact how log data is stored and accessed, affecting security monitoring, query performance, and compliance.
bigquery_options.compliant: Properly configured BigQuery options matching security requirements
bigquery_options.non-compliant: Misconfigured options that impact security monitoring or compliance

use_partitioned_tables.description: By default, Logging creates dated tables based on the log entries' timestamps, e.g. syslog_20170523. With partitioned tables, the date suffix is no longer present and [special query syntax](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/querying-partitioned-tables) has to be used instead. In both cases, tables are sharded based on UTC timezone.
use_partitioned_tables.rationale: Partitioned tables can improve query performance and cost efficiency but require proper query syntax and management.
use_partitioned_tables.compliant: true (for improved performance and cost management)
use_partitioned_tables.non-compliant: false (when partitioned tables are required for compliance or performance)

exclusions.description: Log entries that match any of the exclusion filters are not exported.
exclusions.rationale: Exclusions must be carefully configured to avoid filtering out security-critical log data while properly reducing noise.
exclusions.compliant: Minimal, well-justified exclusions that don't impact security monitoring
exclusions.non-compliant: Overly broad exclusions that filter security-relevant logs or exclusions that could mask malicious activity

name.description: The name of the exclusion. Must be unique within the sink.
name.rationale: Exclusion names should clearly indicate purpose to ensure proper management and auditability.
name.compliant: Descriptive exclusion names following naming conventions

description.description: A description of the exclusion's purpose and what log entries it filters out.
description.rationale: Clear descriptions help ensure proper understanding of what log data is being excluded and why.
description.compliant: Detailed description of exclusion criteria and business justification

filter.description: The filter that determines which log entries to exclude from the sink.
filter.rationale: Exclusion filters must be carefully constructed to avoid excluding security-relevant logs.
filter.compliant: Well-defined filters that exclude only non-security-relevant noise
filter.non-compliant: Overly broad filters that exclude security-critical logs

disabled.description: Whether the exclusion is disabled. If true, the exclusion does not filter any log entries.
disabled.rationale: Exclusion status should match the intended filtering behavior for proper log export management.
disabled.compliant: Properly configured based on exclusion requirements
disabled.non-compliant: Misconfigured exclusion status that impacts log filtering
